title: Can nootropic supplementation improve cognitive function in healthy adults? A systematic review and meta-analysis

Objective performance measures only; MeSH terms on the record include Cognition, Nootropic Agents and Reaction Time.

verifier_correction:
Three corrections, all non-material to the verdict:

(1) COMPASS battery composition is wrong. The researcher lists five/six components ending in "digit span". The record states seven: 1. immediate and delayed word recall, 2. delayed word recognition, 3. delayed picture recognition, 4. Corsi blocks task, 5. DIGIT VIGILANCE (not digit span), 6. Stroop test, 7. choice reaction time. Stroop and choice reaction time were omitted entirely - relevant because they are the executive-function/processing-speed endpoints most likely to move.

(2) Doses ARE stated in the registry, contrary to "no dose should be assumed". Three parallel arms: T1 placebo maltodextrin 2 x 6 g/day; T2 omega-3 fatty acids 2 x 1 g/day (3:1 DHA:EPA) + curcumin 2 x 500 mg/day + citicoline 2 x 500 mg/day + maltodextrin 2 x 6 g/day; T3 the same three plus creatine monohydrate 2 x 5 g/day + guanidinoacetic acid 2 x 1 g/day. title: Impact of Nicotine From Five Variants of a Nicotine Tablet on Attention in Adult Users of Nicotine Pouches: An Exploratory, Randomized, Controlled, Double-blind, Crossover Study
intervention: Dissolvable oral nicotine tablet (mint flavour) at five nicotine contents — 0 mg, 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.5 mg, 2.0 mg — used for approximately 10 minutes, double-blind crossover. This is a true dose-response design, which is unusual and makes it more informative than a single-dose comparison.
population: Adults 19-60, healthy-volunteers flag true, condition listed as 'Attention'. Participants are current non-daily users of nicotine pouches (past 30-day use) who express no desire to quit; excluded if using NRT or cessation medication, if urine cotinine exceeds 500 ng/mL, or if exhaled CO is at least 10 ppm.
